fields.sample_size: federal government investment data on sanitation 2004-2009 (e.g. onerous resources FGTS R$ 15 billion contracted, R$ 6.1 billion disbursed; BNDES/FAT R$ 11.9 billion contracted; non-onerous R$ 40.2 billion committed 2005-2009, R$ 28.3 billion disbursed, 70.4%); no respondent sample
fields.effect_estimate: Federal sanitation investments 2004-2009 did not match the profile of service deficits: resources continued to favour the Southeast and South (already higher coverage) while small municipalities and the North, with the largest deficits, had difficulty accessing funds; fiscal context, macroeconomic policy, access rules and eligibility criteria influenced programme outcomes; patrimonialism, a techno-bureaucratic approach, state weaknesses and permeability to corruption, and weak social movements are cited as constraints. Descriptive quali-quantitative policy analysis.
fields.study_design: quali-quantitative national policy analysis using federal investment data (documentary)
fields.section: Full text: Method; Results (investment volumes by source, Figs 2-3); Discussion; Conclusions
fields.exact_location: Method; Results (investment volumes by source, Figs 2-3); Discussion; Conclusions

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a quali-quantitative analysis of Brazilian federal sanitation investments 2004-2009, read in full text 2026-10-04. Investments favoured better-served regions and did not match deficit profiles; eligibility criteria and access rules disadvantaged small municipalities. Descriptive; no effect estimates.
